answer: Each agent identity must keep its own large storage plot, seeded from its address so no two plots match and none can mirror another. At random moments auditors ask for a few blocks from that plot and expect a reply within seconds, too fast to rebuild them on demand. One honest agent keeps one plot; an operator running fifty fakes must buy and power fifty, so the cost climbs with every extra name like gear hauled up a summit. Clever wording cannot fake storage: the bytes are there, solid as onyx, or the account fails the check.
